newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha slips, middle distillates quiet.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha slips, middle distillates quiet.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were steady to a tad weaker in a quiet market on Friday, traders said.
Second-half July open-spec naphtha was quoted at $212.00/213.00 per tonne. It was sold to a Japanese trading house at $213.00 in late-Thursday dealing.
In spreads, first-half July/second-half July was traded at minus $1.50.

In middle distillates trading, no jet kerosene deals were heard concluded since two Japanese oil firms bought spot South Korean cargoes at about $1.10 and $1.30 per barrel over the mean of Singapore quotes late last month.
Japan's buying interest remained sluggish due to high inventories, traders said.
Levels for spot jet cargoes were notionally assessed at $1.10 to $1.20 over the mean of Singapore quotes.
Term talks between Saudi Arabia and thirteen potential naphtha buyers remained deadlocked, traders said.

They said that although most buyers appeared ready to accept the offer price of $17.00 over the Aramco formula for A-180 naphtha to be lifted at Ras Tanura in the second half of 1997, they were reluctant to pay a $15.00 premium for full-range naphtha. -- Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
